clause_i.reason: For the geometry-dependent repair modes, an observation-free q using only I_t cannot choose the seed-specific missing or false edge across generated seeds: the target fibre is randomized and public segment labels are opaque. The current static screenshot can supply the needed geometric information, so this is a visual dependency rather than a temporal one.

clause_ii.reason: A current screenshot of the static mesh/slices, together with the agent's own prior controls, is sufficient in principle to choose the next simplified repair action; no positive-width sequence of frames is needed. This bounded-window sufficiency does not imply real time because the displayed state does not evolve while the agent waits.

clause_iii.reason: There is no autonomous non-clock task-state evolution from H_t to H_t^tau for any Delta > 0. Waiting leaves the visible geometry, topology, focus, camera, controls, and outcome value unchanged; only event handlers change repair state. The fixed 180-second allowance is only a deadline and cannot supply the required strict loss.

common_visible_process: None. No common visible autonomous process changes the task state or makes a repair action expire or degrade.

pre_run.reason: The mathematical definition already fails clause (iii), so the pre-run threshold cannot change this configuration-level No label.

source_evidence.claim: Difficulty 1 is the two-fibre, six-segment, one-missing-join, one-false-join, seven-slice profile.
The simplified surface uses labelled plane steps, orbit buttons, segment selectors, and opposite-colour seed controls; observation_window_ms is 0 and frames_per_observation is 1.
The runner configuration also has a zero observation window, one frame, a 180-second allowance, and synchronous execution.
The generator consumes the supplied control condition and applies the selected profile parameters rather than the uncontrolled hard/full fallback.
Generation creates seeded static node coordinates and initial/true edge sets, then exports the static mesh, slices, focus, and requirements; it defines no autonomous evolution.
The simplified render exposes plane-step controls, orbit buttons, selectors, seed controls, cut, and certification while the mesh is a canvas view.
State changes and repair events occur in slice, orbit, selection, merge, seed, and cut input handlers; the handlers contain no timer- or idle-driven task transition.
The only asynchronous operation is the result fetch after the visible certification action, which is administrative rather than an autonomous outcome phase.
The complete mechanic stylesheet contains static layout and appearance rules only, with no animation, transition, or keyframe process.

The grader replays the submitted event transcript from the initial topology and changes state only for submitted repair/view events; it grades the final topology and inspection transcript, not elapsed idle time.
The verifier loads the exported result and branch-repair grader; it adds no temporal task rule.
The implementation solver reads the generated truth and performs static observations, orbit, edits, inspections, and certification; it has no autonomous outcome phase.
The shared clock can run an explicit observation window, but this branch mechanic supplies no timer or animation that changes task state during that window.
